I’m afraid I don’t have the ability to call out‑of‑band services directly—so I can’t pull the live VirusTotal record for **reddit.com** myself. What I *can* do is walk you through exactly how you would query the API yourself (or write a quick script) so you’ll see all the same information that the official VT console shows. --- ## Quick Reference – How to Query a Domain via the REST API | Step | What to Do | |------|------------| | 1️⃣ | Build your request URL:
`https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/`
For this case: `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/reddit.com` | | 2️⃣ | Add the header `X-Apikey: ` (`reddit_api_key`). | | 3️⃣ | Send a GET request (HTTPS/JSON). | ### Example Using cURL ```bash curl -XGET \ --header "x-apikey: reddit_api_key" \ https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/reddit.com ``` ### Example Using Python + Requests ```python import requests API_KEY = "reddit_api_key" DOMAIN = "reddit.com" url = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{DOMAIN}" headers = {"x-apikey": API_KEY} resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers) data = resp.json() print(resp.status_code) # Should be 200 OK print(data["meta"]["page_info"]) # Pagination info print(data["attributes"]) ``` If you prefer a higher‑level wrapper: ```bash pip install vt-py ``` ```python from vt import Client client = Client("reddit_api_key") obj = client.get_object(f"/domains/reddit.com") print(obj.last_analysis_stats) print(obj.attributes.ip_addresses) ``` --- ## Typical Fields You’ll See in the Response Below’s a trimmed‑down view of the most useful parts of a typical `/domains/*` payload: | Field | Meaning | |-------|---------| | `last_analysis_date` | Unix timestamp of the latest scan run. | | `last_analysis_results` | Dictionary keyed by AV engine name → result (“malicious”, “harmless”, …). | | `last_analysis_stats` | Aggregated counts per verdict (e.g., `"harmless": 70`, `"malicious": 0`). | | `reputation` | Numeric score (higher = more suspicious). | | `tags` | User‑defined tags attached to the object. | | `whois_information` | Raw WHOIS text block. | | `ip_addresses` | List of IPs resolved for the domain. | | `subdomains` | Array of subdomain objects (each has its own stats). | | `communicating_samples` | Samples that contacted the domain during scanning. | | `related_domains` | Other domains linked to the same samples/IPs. | A full schema reference is available here: [VirusTotal v3 Domains Endpoint](https://developers.virustotal.com/reference/domain) --- ## Common Pitfalls & Tips | Issue | Fix / Tip | |-------|-----------| | **401 Unauthorized** | Double‑check that the key hasn’t expired and that you’re sending it in the exact header name `x-apikey`. | | **Rate limiting (429)** | VT allows ~4–5 queries/sec for free keys. If you hit limits, add exponential backoff or upgrade to a paid plan. | | **Missing subdomains** | Some domains may not return subdomains unless you’ve previously scanned them. Use the “Subdomains” tab in the UI first. | | **Large responses** | For very active sites, pagination appears under `links.next`; iterate until exhausted. | --- ## Next Steps 1. Run one of the snippets above locally. 2. Inspect the returned JSON; copy/paste into a pretty‑printer (e.g., [jsonformatter.org]()). 3. Look at the `last_analysis_stats` field—it gives you a quick health check. Feel free to paste the raw output here if you’d like help interpreting specific values!
